gen-irish-grover-gf-piazzolla: Lowercase that nearly matches its capitals gives Piazzolla a stately, upright look. Irish Grover is the one to lean on for sturdy, friendly bulk, while Piazzolla does its best work as a classic serif with authority.
gen-irish-grover-gf-scope-one: Irish Grover's tall lowercase makes every word look sturdy and oversized, with joins that taper only slightly. And Scope One gives it a refined partner, its big x-height and spilling counters keeping everything open.
gen-irish-grover-gf-slabo-13px: Chunky yet friendly, Irish Grover has softly varied strokes that stay solid and readable. Slabo 13px, a text serif with large open counters, is happiest at a modest size, so a small suggestion is to let it stay small.
gen-irish-grover-gf-suwannaphum: Dignified is the mood Suwannaphum sets, with a tall x-height like a squared-off woodblock letter. Suwannaphum, a classic serif, is the steady reader here, while Irish Grover handles the fun, organic, mid-contrast shouting.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-glegoo: Loud and cheerful, with ink that looks poured. Glegoo, a text serif with big counters and wide-mouthed curves, is the one that does the quiet, refined reading, while Luckiest Guy does the shouting.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-hanuman: Luckiest Guy is a jolly shout. Hanuman, a high-waisted serif with wide-set terminals on its s, follows with traditional restraint, so the ballpoint-plain headline line and the finer text sit comfortably together.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-kadwa: Kadwa reads openly, its curves left unclosed and its x-height larger than usual. And Luckiest Guy, with no visible difference between up and side strokes, gives that serif a loud, cheerful start.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noticia-text: Luckiest Guy sets a cheerful, loud tone, its horizontals matching its verticals in thickness, then hands over to a literary body. Noticia Text, a classic serif, supplies the dignity.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-piazzolla: A high mean line and a look of glass tubing bent into letters make Luckiest Guy instantly recognizable. Piazzolla, a text serif with an open e, would carry a long passage with refined, authoritative ease.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-pridi: Poured ink in one weight, with rounds and stems alike, is what defines Luckiest Guy. Pridi, a classic serif with proud small letters, handles the careful reading.
